title: A renewal plan's value in NPV-equivalent dollars

blocks.text: A water utility plans when to renew its mains. Each main may start in one or more years, and the model has a binary start variable `x[(main, year)]` for each. For every possible start the asset team has computed three benefits in `benefits[(main, year)]`: breaks avoided, leakage avoided in megalitres, and NPV in $k. The board has fixed a reference swing and a weight for each measure, and it wants every number in the plan's report in **$k of NPV-equivalent**: the NPV that would earn the same value.

Write `coefficients(benefits, reference, weights)` in `renewals.py`, returning each start's value in $k of NPV-equivalent, and `objective(x, coefficient)`, the plan's value as one MathOpt linear expression in the start variables. The tests read the objective on fixed plans with `mathopt.evaluate_expression`; nothing is solved.
The measures' keys, the same in `benefits`, `reference` and `weights`, are `"breaks"`, `"leakage"` and `"npv"`; the financial measure, the one that sets the dollar conversion, is `"npv"`.

Write $`v_{i,t}`$ in the notation of lesson 7.4.4 first, then the factor that turns it into dollars. The references are the board's, fixed for the planning cycle: a new candidate must not change any other main's value. About six lines.

cases.says: each main and start year gets its value in $k of NPV-equivalent, worked out by hand
the objective expression, evaluated on a fixed plan, is the sum of the chosen starts' coefficients, and 0 for no starts
a main with two possible start years gets a coefficient for each from that year's benefits
a new candidate with benefits beyond the references changes no other coefficient and may score above them
